answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with aged identities: a new identity starts with zero earning power and must accumulate honest attestations across several epochs before it can claim rewards. Like timber that only gains strength after seasons of growth, trust must be seasoned over time, so an attacker minting a thousand fresh identities gains nothing today. No ivory-tower shortcut exists: the ledger records each identity's history on basalt-solid ground, so mass-created clones stay visibly young and worthless while real agents compound standing.
